back: The movement of people from one place to another to live, usually for at least a year.
A person forced to flee their country because of war, violence or persecution, who cannot safely return.
A person who has applied for protection as a refugee in another country and is awaiting a decision.
A person who moves voluntarily to find work or a higher income.
Push: problems at the origin (unemployment, drought, conflict). Pull: attractions of the destination (jobs, services, safety).
Remittances: money or goods sent home. Brain drain: loss of skilled workers through emigration.
Push: economic decline after about 2000, unemployment, hyperinflation 2007-2008. Pull: jobs and wages next door. Main crossing: Beitbridge.
Skills-based visas, work permits, border controls, refugee camps, aid to origin countries, integration programmes.
